clues: This city sits on the west bank of a wide river, close to where a smaller river joins it. Ships can sail up this river from the sea.
Winters here are cold, and snow can pile deep in a storm. Great storms off the Atlantic can dump heavy snow on the town at once.
In 1797, the state capital was shifted to this river town for good. Lawmakers had moved it from place to place for years before that.
This river town was chartered in 1686, and it still holds that charter today. It is the longest-held city charter in the whole land.
New York's lawmakers meet in this city, and the state governor works here too. It speaks and acts for the whole state as its capital.
